title: Verdikt SLA v1
description: The provider-authored document stored verbatim in the `sla` ENS text record on <slug>.verdikt.eth. Validated by @verdikt/sla's own JSON Schema subset, so this file is executable rather than documentation that can drift.

clauses.description: At least one. An empty clause list would make every call PASS, including a 5xx, which is why it is rejected rather than treated as 'promises nothing'.

minMinorUnits.description: Decimal integer string. JSON has no bigint and a float would break the integer-only comparison the spec requires.

oneOf.title: semantic clause
oneOf.description: A promise about what the response *says*, judged on dispute by a GenLayer Intelligent Contract rather than per call by CRE (docs/roadmap/genlayer.md). `evaluate` recognises it and always passes it: the deterministic engine is pure by invariant and cannot judge meaning, and refusing to parse the document would be worse — it would fall back to status-only and lose every deterministic clause the provider declared alongside it.

criteria.description: The binding judgment text, in plain language. Its own field rather than a reuse of `description`, which stays decorative on every clause type including this one: a reader has to be able to tell what the provider promised from what it merely explained. Frozen into the claim at filing time, so editing the SLA mid-dispute cannot change what is being judged.
